newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Dec palm oil output down 17.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Dec palm oil output down 17.4 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in December is estimated to have fallen by 17.4 percent to 630,000 tonnes from November, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Tuesday.
Wong put end-December palm oil stocks at 805,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 955,965 tonnes at end-November.
Exports in December is estimated at 660,000 tonnes against PORLA's 632,441 tonnes in November.

Wong said in a report that the decline in production was caused partly by poorer than expected output in eastern Sabah state because of monsoon rains and floods which hit the state in the last week of December. He estimated production for the whole of 1996 at 8.38 million tonnes, an increase of 7.3 percent or 568,000 tonnes over 1995.
Wong put crude palm oil stocks at the end of December at 485,000 tonnes and processed palm oil stocks at 320,000 tonnes.
The higher exports reflected mainly increased offtake by Islamic countries in anticipation of growth in consumption during the Ramadan period in January/February, he said.
